rule: mixed: the rule is fireable and every participant is covered, but 'from wraiths' is filed in the origin slot, which reads as the warding coming out of the wraiths rather than as protection against them. One word fixes it: 'Ground feathers ward lanterns against wraiths.'
texts: bad: 'the Keepers' mints one specific anonymous band of keepers, and the rule's condition then demands that exact band, so it can only ever fire on this sentence itself and never on a later scattering by any Keeper. Use a singular indefinite subject (and 'against' for the threat, which otherwise lands in the origin slot): 'When a Keeper scatters ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths.'

bad: same defect — 'the Keepers' pins the condition to one specific anonymous keeper group, so no other spreading can ever trigger the rule; separately, 'ground' ends up said of the bundle of feathers as a single object rather than of the feathers themselves. Rewrite as 'If a Keeper spreads ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths.'
good. a fireable generic denial — no wraith approaches a warded lantern — with 'warded' kept as a property of the lantern rather than folded into the noun.

mixed: on its own the rule is fireable and faithful, but here 'ground feathers' is fused into a single kind symbol while the headline rule and the 'stale' sentence keep 'ground' as a separate property of ordinary feathers, so the fresh rule and the stale rule never range over the same things; the singular 'a lantern' also differs from the plural object the other two use. Bring the wording into line with them: 'Fresh ground feathers ward lanterns.'

mixed: the denial itself is right, but 'a lantern' is an indefinite that should introduce an actual lantern and instead comes out as the bare kind — the same slot its 'fresh' twin fills with a real lantern, so the two halves of the contrast do not line up. Writing the object as a plural makes the bare kind the correct encoding and matches the headline rule: 'Stale ground feathers do not ward lanterns.'
